prompt: Why does the payment-retry condition have `duration = "600s"`?

choices.text: Cloud Monitoring needs ten minutes to compute a sum
choices.why: Sums are per minute; the duration is a choice.

choices.text: So one busy minute does not fire it
choices.why: Right. It must stay over five for ten minutes.

choices.text: To delay every notification by ten minutes after recovery
choices.why: It delays the firing, not anything after recovery.

choices.text: Because log metrics arrive ten minutes late
choices.why: They arrive within about a minute.

prompt: A failure counter has no data on a quiet night. Which `evaluation_missing_data` is right, and why?

choices.text: ACTIVE: missing data may mean the service is down
choices.why: For this counter, missing data is the normal good night; it would page every night.

choices.text: INACTIVE: no point means no failures
choices.why: Right. Silence is the good case here.

choices.text: NO_OP: keep the last state
choices.why: It could leave an incident open long after it ended.

choices.text: None: missing data is never evaluated
choices.why: The setting exists because it is.

prompt: What is the metric type of the log-based counter `shop/payment_retries`?
hint: User-defined log metrics have their own prefix.

choices.text: custom.googleapis.com/shop/payment_retries
choices.why: That prefix is for metrics a program writes.

choices.text: run.googleapis.com/shop/payment_retries
choices.why: run.googleapis.com is Cloud Run's own metrics.

choices.text: logging.googleapis.com/user/shop/payment_retries
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: shop/payment_retries, with no prefix
choices.why: Every metric type has a full name.

prompt: Why does the payment-retry policy notify the tickets channel and not on-call?

choices.text: Pub/Sub channels are cheaper than e-mail
choices.why: Price is not the reason.

choices.text: It needs action this week, not now
choices.why: Right. A page promises that somebody must act now.

choices.text: WARNING severity cannot be sent by e-mail
choices.why: Any severity can go to any channel.

choices.text: On-call is only for log-based alerts
choices.why: The uptime and burn-rate pages are metric alerts.

prompt: In pages.py's month, how many notifications did anybody act on?
hint: The last column of the total row.

choices.why: That is all of them.
Those arrived at night.
Right. Eleven out of 76.
Those closed within ten minutes.

prompt: Why delete `cpu above 80%` rather than raise its threshold?

choices.text: A cause, never acted on by anybody
choices.why: Right. The SLI already says whether users are failing.

choices.text: Cloud Run does not report CPU
choices.why: It does; the metric is real and still not a symptom.

choices.text: High CPU is always a bug in the code
choices.why: High CPU is usually just a busy service.

choices.text: Policies cannot have thresholds above 80
choices.why: Any threshold is allowed.

prompt: If `cpu above 80%` (61 notifications) is deleted, how many notifications would the month have had?
A policy's notifications last month were all closed within ten minutes with no action. What is the right reading?

choices.text: The team is not taking alerts seriously
choices.why: The team is responding correctly to noise.

choices.text: The policy is noise, whatever it was created for
choices.why: Right. Fix it like a defect.

choices.text: It works: incidents are being resolved quickly
choices.why: They closed themselves; nobody resolved anything.

choices.text: auto_close is too short
choices.why: They closed because the condition cleared, not by auto_close.

prompt: Which of these belong on a page to the person on call? Choose all that apply.
hint: A symptom users feel, needing action now.

choices.text: The uptime check failing from two regions
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A fast burn of the error budget
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Memory use above 70%
choices.why: No. A cause; a dashboard item.

choices.text: Payment retries a little above normal
choices.why: No. A ticket for working hours.

prompt: The policy field whose text arrives with the notification, saying what to do, is `___`.
Put the review of a noisy policy in order.
items: Count its notifications over the month
Check how many anybody acted on
Ask whether it is a symptom users feel
Delete it, move it to tickets, or keep it
trap: Deleting before counting is the slip: it might be the one policy that catches real failures.

prompt: Match each of the shop's policies to its channel.
A week brings four night pages. What does the shop do on Monday?
hint: More than two triggers a review.

choices.text: Add a third person to the rotation
choices.why: More people share the noise; they do not remove it.

choices.text: Mute every policy for a week
choices.why: That would hide real failures too.

choices.text: Review the policy of each page
choices.why: Right. A needless page is a defect in a policy.

choices.text: Nothing, unless a page was missed
choices.why: Waiting for a missed page is waiting for the damage.
